A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, determine which represented billed revenue is tied to counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with source-native identifiers and invoice attributes.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entity_kinds: counterparties (as named on invoices and contracts)
contractual clauses bearing on change of control or assignment
excluded_from_universe: revenue not represented in billing sources
contracts or invoices outside the data room
counterparties with no represented billing or contract footprint in scope

world_eligible: invoice exists with id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status as recorded in sources
contract exists with identifier as it appears in sources
contract contains textual clauses (consent/notice on change of control; termination on change of control; consent/notice before assignment including affiliate-only or competitor-prohibition variants)
contract temporal/status facts (e.g., whether a statement of work is expired vs in force)
counterparty names as they appear on invoices and contracts
purpose_dependent: whether a clause counts as acquisition-relevant under Purpose A policy
whether a contract counts as active for this purpose (expired SOW is not active)
whether an invoice qualifies for inclusion (must be represented billed revenue associated—asserted or unresolved—with a counterparty whose active contract has acquisition-relevant conditions)
invoice-to-contract association disposition: asserted vs unresolved

epistemic_requirements: Report identifiers exactly as they appear in authoritative sources.
Do not treat missing or uncertain identity linkage as a negative contractual finding.
If billed name and contract counterparty cannot be confidently associated, mark association unresolved rather than omitting the invoice or asserting the join.
Positive association requires confidence; absence of confidence is not evidence of non-association.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: invoice is in scope for reporting but the link between billed name and governing contract counterparty is not confidently established

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: every invoice that qualifies under Purpose A inclusion policy must appear in invoices
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: for each included invoice, report invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status, contract_id, and association
completeness_expectations.identifier_fidelity: contract_id and invoice_id as they appear in sources (no silent renaming)
completeness_expectations.unresolved_explicitness: uncertain joins must be surfaced as association=unresolved, not dropped

acquisition_relevant_condition_kinds: requires consent or notice on a change of control
permits termination upon a change of control
requires consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or assignment prohibited to a competitor
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_threshold: an expired statement of work is not an active contract
purpose_specific_policies.inclusion_rule: include invoice when represented billed revenue is associated (asserted or unresolved) with a counterparty whose active contract contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition

association_mapping.unresolved: join required for reporting but not confidently established

non_policies: missing identity is not a negative contractual finding
do not omit qualifying invoices solely because association is unresolved

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, reconcile represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, state whether it is confidently the same legal counterparty as another record or remains unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entity_kinds: commercially relevant names and records spanning CRM accounts, billed names, registry rows, and contract parties

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

world_eligible: CRM account records with ids and names as sourced
registry company rows with company numbers and registered names
contract party names keyed by contract filename
exact legal-form string variants of the same registered name (mechanical normalization candidates)
purpose_dependent: whether two records are confidently the same legal counterparty (SAME_ENTITY)
whether two records are confidently distinct legal entities (DISTINCT)
which pairwise links are required to connect CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and registry candidate for a commercial relationship

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical sameness.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Permit explicit unresolved identity; missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (DISTINCT) judgment.
DISTINCT requires establishing evidence of distinctness, not mere absence of a positive merge.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: insufficient evidence to assert SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT for the left/right pair

completeness_expectations.link_coverage: include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship
completeness_expectations.pair_orientation: emit directed left/right pairs per schema; sort for stable output
completeness_expectations.identifier_typing: all endpoints use the mandated crm:/billing:/registry:/contract: forms

merge_policy.permitted_mechanical: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name
merge_policy.forbidden_automatic: merge on fuzzy or trade-name similarity alone
merge_policy.distinct_registry_entities: similar trade names do not imply SAME_ENTITY

purpose_specific_policies.required_link_pattern: for each commercially relevant relationship, connect CRM account ↔ billed name ↔ governing contract ↔ registry candidate(s)

epistemic_dispositions.SAME_ENTITY: confident positive identification as one legal counterparty
epistemic_dispositions.DISTINCT: confident positive identification as different legal counterparties

non_policies: absence of SAME_ENTITY is not DISTINCT
similarity is not sufficient for SAME_ENTITY

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under Purpose C criteria, including open invoices and qualifying contract obligations, using Purpose B identifier forms.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entity_kinds: contract obligation clauses (exclusivity, auto-renewal, rolling term)
universe_scope.identifier_forms: same as Purpose B (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:)

required_output_shape.ordering: sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row

world_eligible: invoice open/closed status and ids as sourced
contract active/expired status and renewal/term mechanics as sourced
presence of exclusivity, auto-renewal, or rolling-term language in contracts
counterparty identifiers and contract ids as sourced
purpose_dependent: whether a counterparty is commercially dependent under the two-part Purpose C test
whether a current commercial relationship exists (open invoice OR active auto-renew/rolling contract)
whether obligation_kinds are drawn from the allowed enum for dependency counting
dependency status: dependent vs unresolved when identity joins are insufficient

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report dependency as unresolved rather than false/non-dependent.
Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
A one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not establish dependency.
Use Purpose B identifier forms for counterparty; unresolved identity propagates to unresolved dependency.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: dependency cannot be confidently asserted or denied because required identity or join evidence is missing

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: report each counterparty-contract combination that is dependent or unresolved under Purpose C policy
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: counterparty, contract_id, open_invoice_ids, obligation_kinds, status for each dependency row
completeness_expectations.cross_purpose_dependency: counterparty identifiers must align with Purpose B forms; leverage Purpose B identity judgments where needed

commercial_dependency_test.part_1_current_relationship: open invoice OR active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
commercial_dependency_test.part_2_qualifying_obligation: active contract contains exclusivity commitment, term auto-renewal, or rolling term continuing unless notice is given

exclusions: expired contracts do not create current dependency
one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create dependency

obligation_kind_policy.sorting: obligation_kinds sorted ascending within each dependency row

status_mapping.dependent: both parts of the commercial dependency test satisfied with confident joins
status_mapping.unresolved: test outcome indeterminate due to unresolved identity or insufficient join evidence

non_policies: unresolved identity is not equivalent to non-dependent
historical-only billing without active contractual footing does not satisfy part 1
